To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
cytochrome oxidase is a proton pump and the stoichiometry of this process is 0.9.

ferrocytochromec oxidase reconstituted into vesicles ejects protons at a rate of approx. 0-9 per oxidized molecule of cytochrome c, and that this ejection is abolished by the presence of a protonophore.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the elucidation of the mechanism of proton translocation in the cytochrome c-oxidase system, a process which is of central importance to the energy-conservation mechanism of the mitochondrial respiratory chain.
the mechanism of proton translocation by the cytochrome c-cytochrome c oxidoreductase (cytochrome c oxidases).
the elucidation of the molecular mechanisms of proton pumping in cytochrome c-oxidase, and in particular the role played by the protonatable residues in the protein.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
cytochrome oxidase is a proton pump.
cytochrome oxidase is a proton pump and not merely a hydrogen atom pump.
cytochrome oxidase acts as an electrogenic proton pump.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have been able to show that proton translocation can occur with a reconstituted oxidase-containing system, that it is dependent on turnover of the oxidase and that it is dependent upon the ratio of enzyme and lipid employed in the reconstitution.
cytochrome oxidase can act as a proton pump when it is reconstituted in lipid vesicles, and that the stoichiometry is 4H+/4e-.
cytochrome oxidase is a proton pump and not an electrogenic pump.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the reconstituted vesicles can be used as a model for studying proton translocation in cytochrome c-oxidase.
it is important to control the number of turnovers when studying proton translocation in this system.
the reconstituted vesicle system is a powerful tool for investigating the proton-translocating activity of cytochrome c-oxidase.
